correctness.rationale: For compact invariant μ of the Michelson flow x′=y, y′=z, z′=c²−y−x²/2, testing L on antiderivatives of continuous functions of x,y,z yields E[y|x]=0, E[z|y]=0, and E[x²+2y|z]=2c². Marginal expectations imply E[x²]=2c²; Var(x)=2c²−m² and the equilibrium rigidity follow. Any nonequilibrium stationary μ must have positive mass with x² both below and above 2c²; continuity forces periodic threshold crossings. Q=x²+2y gives Q−2c²=−2z′, hence Var(Q)=4E[(z′)²] and Cov(z,Q)=0. Bounded complete trajectories establish the zero-defect rigidity. An independent exact rational test gave Q−2c²=−1109/225 at x=7/5,y=−2/3,c²=25/9 and equals −2z′. Correctness is supported; no finite experiment is used as a proof of an infinite-time stationary law.
